sentences.text: The genus name Halisaurus translates to “ocean lizard”.
Individuals of this genus reached about 3 to 4 metres (10 to 13 feet) in length, which is small for mosasaurs.
A BBC program suggested that Halisaurus hid in underwater caves to ambush small animals such as Hesperornis.
Halisaurus auriculatus was described as a new species in 2026.
The type locality is the Dakhla Formation in Egypt, and the species is known only from that country.
Halisaurus auriculatus is a valid mosasaur species belonging to the subfamily Halisaurinae.
Phylogenetic analysis places it in a polytomy with H. hebae and the clade formed by H. arambourgi and H. platyspondylus.
This species lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian age.
The broader genus Halisaurus persisted from the Santonian to the Danian, roughly 85.7 to 61.66 million years ago.
The coexistence of two morphologically distinct halisaurine species in the Dakhla Shale has been interpreted as possible niche partitioning among these mosasaurs.
